messages:
alex: heads up — console fired a p95 latency alert for streaming endpoints around 07:16 UTC. looks concentrated on the new sticky-routing canary. dashboard shows a ~400ms jump for ~6m. is this real or just metric noise?
maria: thanks. which metric exactly? p95 server-side or client-observed?
alex: server-side p95 token_emit_latency per-route (route=stream-resume). dashboard panel: https://console/redwood/d/streaming?panel=emit_latency
ops-bot: ALERT: streaming-p95-high (severity: medium)
ops-bot: sample log snippet attached: `proxy=edge-12 route=stream-resume latency_ms=412 tags="sticky_canary=true" trace_id=tr-9a3b`
jordan: I saw similar during canary last night but we thought it was sampling/telemetry double-counting. this looks sustained though. did the canary change batching or kv-cache behavior?
sam: quick note — the canary changed route selection to prefer same-edge sticky leases instead of hop-by-hop; that adds a proxy hop in the rare sticky-failover path. could explain +300ms in worst-case.
maria: can we correlate with prefix cache misses? if sticky goes to an edge without warm kv cache we can hit cold kv reads. any cache-miss metric spikes?
alex: checking. cache_miss_rate doesn't move much, but kv_read_latency has a tail bump aligning with the window. also some 502s in one edge (edge-12).
jordan: exact repro: curl SSE with header `X-Resume-Token: t:tr-9a3b` that forces resume path. try: ```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "X-Resume-Token: t:tr-9a3b" https://api.redwood/stream
```
sam: tried that locally against canary cluster — saw an extra proxy hop due to health-check switch. sequence: client -> edge-12 -> internal-proxy -> runtime. internal-proxy adds ~200-300ms for TLS and muxing.
maria: ugh. that explains it. console alerts are aggregating at p95 and not attributing multi-hop overhead. we should tag metrics by hop_count and expose p50/p95 for single-hop vs multi-hop.
alex: proposal: temporary alert suppression for canary edge-12 to prevent noisy flapping while we fix attribution. long-term: add hop_count label and surface in the streaming latency dashboard.
jordan: also add high-cardinality `sticky_canary` tag only for debug sampling — we can't keep that in prod metrics. maybe add it to traces and sample logs.
sam: agree. short term: I'll add a rate-limited debug sampling to the canary (10rps) and push a metric that breaks latency by hop_count.
maria: I'll update the dashboard panels to split by hop_count and add an annotation layer for canary rollouts. ops, please mute the alert for 30m?
ops-bot: ACTION: muting streaming-p95-high for channel eng-platform for 30m per request from maria
alex: next steps: 1) sam add hop_count metric + sampled traces (today) 2) maria update dashboard + alert to exclude sampled debug tags (today) 3) jordan review routing policy to avoid proxy hop on sticky path (post-mortem) 4) ops keep muted unless new edges show issues
maria: also adding a lightweight console UX note so SREs can see when canary rollouts coincide with spikes. small banner in the streaming dashboard.
sam: started PR: add hop_count label from edge proxy, and trace bridge for resume tokens. will link in 10m.
jordan: nice. if we need to rollback canary we should automate that via the console rollout UI so humans don't have to mute alerts.
alex: agreed. thanks all. updating incident channel with summary. :thumbsup:
